text:
alice nguyen: FYI we hit repeated primary-model saturation on eu-dedicated yesterday for tier=pro, thinking about automatic variant fallback that respects tenant QoS and quotas :thinking:
raj patel: Can you outline the failure mode? was it sudden burst or slow growth?
emily carter: It was a surge from a single tenant's batch processing + long sequences. primary GPU pool hit slot cap, requests queued and tail latencies blew up. infra-bot posted the alert around 03:12 UTC. :alarm_clock:
alice nguyen: Proposal: add a per-tenant circuit-breaker that triggers variant fallback when we see sustained slot occupancy > 85% for N seconds, but only if fallback variant has compatible tokenization and deterministic-ish output (i.e., caller opted-in or tier=pro+).
raj patel: I like circuit-breaker idea. Questions: how do we avoid oscillation if the fallback is slower on some prompts? Also need per-model warmup/cold-cache penalty accounted for.
tom harris: Suggest smoothing: use EWMA of slot_util and a minimum cool-down window of 60s. Also mark fallback events in telemetry with reason codes: SATURATION, QUIESCED, QUOTA_EXCEEDED.
emily carter: We also need an API-level opt-out header for customers that want strict model pinning, e.g., `X-Model-Fallback: disabled` or `X-Prefer-Primary: true`. Default should be allowed for platform-managed fallbacks.
sasha kovalev: Console UX: show per-tenant fallback history, fallback ratio, and a toggle to prefer consistent output over availability. On rollouts page show a timeline with fallback spikes overlayed. :eyes:
alice nguyen: Agree. For implementation idea, router will evaluate candidate variants in this order: (1) same-arch compatible quantized variant in same region, (2) compatible next-best model in same tier, (3) dedicated-to-hosted spill for soft-fail. We should expose a policy JSON for teams to customize. Example:
```
{"fallback_policy":"auto","threshold_pct":"85","window_s":"30","prefer_tiers":["pro","standard"],"max_fallbacks_per_min":"5","opt_out_header":"X-Model-Fallback"}
```
raj patel: Small nit: keep numeric types as numbers in the internal proto, but in this JSON UI example strings OK. Also we need to ensure fallback respects token-limit and function-calling capabilities; we can't reroute to a tiny model for function-calling requests.
emily carter: Telemetry: we need these metrics per-route/tenant/model variant: fallback_count, fallback_latency_delta, fallback_success_rate, pre-fallback_slot_util, post-fallback_slot_util. Hook these into console alerts and anomaly detection.
tom harris: Operational safety: when fallback triggers, mark the tenant as "on-fallback" and reduce autoscaler aggression to avoid thrashing. After cool-down and util<50%, allow sticky return to primary if slot pre-warm passes.
sasha kovalev: UX question: should the console allow manual quiesce of fallback for a tenant? That seems risky but could be useful for debugging. Maybe a gated action with audit log.
alice nguyen: Audit logs + required justification sound good. Also add a per-tenant cap for how often we can fallback per day to avoid quiet degradation of prompt quality.
raj patel: Edge case: multi-stage requests (tool calling) — fallback could break chains. Maybe for multi-call sequences require a session pin to primary or use conservative rules.
emily carter: Could add a session header `X-Session-Fallback-Allowed: false` and SDKs could surface it.
infra-bot: deploy-bot: rollout started for router/v2 (staged) at 1768883200, feature-flag `auto_variant_fallback` enabled for 10% tenants in eu region.
tom harris: Let's roll to 10% and collect metrics for 24h. Need dashboards: fallback_ratio by tenant tier, median latency delta, quality_regressions flagged by eval hooks.
alice nguyen: Action items: 1) raj to draft router circuit-breaker PR with EWMA logic (ETA 2d). 2) emily to spec telemetry fields + console panels (ETA 3d). 3) sasha to mock console toggle + audit flow (ETA 4d). 4) tom to own canary rollout and alert thresholds (ETA 2d). I'll schedule a quick sync after initial canary. :thumbsup:
